frozen: 2026-11-24 night, after reading V2 (../tensorboard-2026-11-24/) and the real rows, before any of the three tabs was built. Weights and anchors are the AI's reading of Zach's ask; revise them freely.

requirements.name: Answers a question the three tabs cannot
requirements.why: "Are there any more tabs we want to add to that outer view? we have overview, targets and runs." A fourth tab earns its place only if it answers a decision Overview (the League, Speed sweeps), Targets and Runs leave open. A sibling lane is redesigning Overview, so a tab that re-draws the League is wasted.
requirements.passCondition: The tab's question is one Zach acts on (ship a config, trust or fix the twin, collect data or retune in a region) and no other tab shows its answer without manual cross-referencing.

anchors.1: Re-draws what the League, Targets or Runs already show.
anchors.3: A new angle, but the next move it points to is vague.
anchors.5: A decision no other tab answers, and the tab names the next move (which config, which targets, which region).

requirements.name: One calm answer first, detail on demand
requirements.why: Zach's UI rule: "one calm answer first, detail on demand"; tabs titled as questions ("Where?" -> "Where is the error?" is better); plain-word labels, angles in degrees, amber/red only for problems.
requirements.passCondition: The first panel states the answer in one sentence with its numbers and n; the detail (distribution, per config, the worst cases) sits under it; labels are plain words; no colour signals a problem that is not one.

anchors.1: A wall of charts; the reader must work out the answer.
anchors.3: The answer is there but not first, or jargon / unexplained colour.
anchors.5: One sentence answers it at a glance; every figure under it says what it aggregates; colours explained.

requirements.name: Every number from the real rows, recounts with the rail
requirements.why: Runs are atomic and the rail filters runs; every tab shows what is left. A tab whose numbers ignore the rail breaks the workbench's one promise.
requirements.passCondition: From all 18,507 runs to one rail pick, the tab's headline and figures change, and both states equal an independent oracle computed in Python from the same rows (check.json).

anchors.1: Fixed numbers, or numbers nobody can trace to rows.
anchors.3: Recounts, but some figure ignores a facet, or no oracle.
anchors.5: Recounts on every facet that can matter, before/after equal to the oracle, the rule named on each figure.

requirements.name: Drills to the target view with the runs it is about
requirements.why: V2's link: a row drills to the target view with keep= (the runs, checked) and back= (the workbench URL with its filter); Open in Rerun there sends the checked runs.
requirements.passCondition: A row or point of the tab opens common/target.html with keep= exactly the runs that row is about and back= this workbench URL with its filter and tab.

anchors.1: No drill, or the target view opens with the wrong runs.
anchors.3: Drills, but keeps every run of the target, or loses the way back.
anchors.5: keep= is exactly the row's runs (a pair, an A/B match-up, the runs through a cell), back= returns to this tab with the filter.

requirements.name: Stock parts, small named gaps
requirements.why: "we don't need to reinvent the wheel": data-ui's <data-workbench> + .base views and traj_compare's coverage grids; a missing feature is a named gap with the exact ask, never a patch to data-ui or traj_compare/src.
requirements.passCondition: The tab is a .base page of stock views where data-ui can draw it; host JS only where it cannot, each such place named in NOTES.md with the ask.

anchors.3: Stock views, but a large host layer or an unnamed workaround.
anchors.5: Stock views end to end; derived rows built by a script; every gap named with its ask.

gates.name: Real data, labelled
gates.condition: Every row comes from the bench payloads (V2's rows, data/<site>.js, the bench's targets/<slug>.js and references); derived rows are built by build_tabs.py from those; nothing is invented, and anything proposed is labelled.

gates.name: V2 plus one tab, one local command
gates.condition: Overview, Targets and Runs are V2's unchanged; the new tab is the fourth; served by serve.py on 127.0.0.1:8852, no CDN.

gates.name: Recount proved
gates.condition: check.json holds the tab's numbers unfiltered and after the scenario's one rail pick, they differ, and each equals the Python oracle.

gates.name: Drill works
gates.condition: A row of the new tab opens the target view with keep= and back=; the target view is ready with that selection.

gates.name: Clean
gates.condition: No console errors, no sideways scroll at 1440 x 900; the rail drags, is remembered and folds, as in V2.
